cells.tense: You meet what shows up, and the deciding happens right there in the open.
cells.ask: When the next thing lands today, say your call on it out loud in one sentence, then take the single step you actually mean and let that stand until something new arrives.
cells.core:
You meet what shows up. Not later, not after a committee meeting in your head — it lands and you move, and the moving is clean because you're actually here for it. Where you decide, things go. Where there's a next step to take, you take it, and the people around you feel the difference between a plan and someone who means it.

What feeds this is the other motion: stopping to listen the way a beginner listens, letting what you don't know yet stay unknown for a minute and be interesting. The charge in you doesn't need protecting from that. It gets sharper when it's fed by real contact instead of speed. Keep the meeting and the deciding on the same day, and the momentum starts carrying weight.

cells.tense: You are braced against something that has not arrived and cannot be written in advance.
cells.ask: Take what is actually here today rather than the version you've already rehearsed, and act on that one alone; leave tomorrow's version unwritten until it shows up, and see how much of the push was for it.
cells.core:
You're ahead of what's here. Something is coming, and you have already settled its shape, argued it, defended it — so today gets spent fighting a meeting that hasn't happened and a consequence that hasn't arrived. The push is real. It just isn't landing on anything. Every exchange becomes a chance to make the future come out right, and the actual thing in front of you keeps being the smaller part of the conversation.

When the pressure lets up, things make sense in your presence — a call that lands because it fits what's actually there, structure that serves what it organizes. That isn't gone. It's behind the bracing.

Take the floor as it is under you today. One rehearsal is enough. Handle what's on the table, then close it, and see what the day still needs once the imagined version stops driving.

cells.tense: You are holding what arrives at the threshold, meeting the present late.
cells.ask: Pick the smallest thing in front of you today — a message, an errand, someone else's ask — and take one physical action on it before the day ends, so the next small thing gets met on time.
cells.core:
Decisions are not what's missing. Hesitation is where you're living. What comes near gets held at the threshold while you wait for a clearer signal, and the waiting has become the answer — so what's already here stays outside and the day moves past you. The sense that things go somewhere once you're in them is not this. Nothing is being met.

That doesn't mean push harder into the stopped place; that just drains it further. It means giving the moving part of you something solid and small to move through — a decision made in real material, where you can see the result. One task, done out loud, in the world. The energy goes into the doing, and the meeting comes back with it.

Big changes aren't required today. One thing actually crossed is.

cells.tense: You are moving things whole already and calling it where you happened to be standing.
cells.ask: Name one decision you've been calling someone else's call or plain necessity — say under whose hands it actually moved — and put your own yes or no on the next similar one before it drifts.
cells.core:
You're deciding and moving things whole, but you're telling it as if the room, the schedule, or someone else is what sets the direction. It keeps working — things go — which is why nothing gets called yours. The force is not the problem. The one thing outside the working part is calling it yours when you do it.

What the shape of this needs isn't a harder push. It's knowing what to release and what to keep — the sense that a thing ended because it had to, trusted from where you stand. Under the framing, endings are already happening and landing; you're just narrating them as if they were happening to you.

So this is a small bookkeeping change. Next time you're deciding, note the hand doing it. Call it yours and set it down no differently.

That's the whole move. The moment the marking catches up, the line becomes one you run instead of one you follow.
